title: AitpRevocationList
description: AITP v0.3 signed revocation snapshot (JCS embedded-signature profile; its serialization is unchanged by the JWS migration, though its signing input changed in v0.2 — see `signature` below) — the response served by an issuing peer's `ListRevoked` HTTPS endpoint (RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5). Lists every TCT JTI the issuer has revoked. Cached by consuming peers per `expires_at`; an empty `entries` array is itself a meaningful signed assertion that nothing has been revoked since the last snapshot, defending against an attacker that suppresses fresher snapshots to roll back revocations.

issuer.description: The issuing peer's AID. MUST equal the `issuer` of every TCT covered by `entries`.

published_at.description: Unix timestamp when this snapshot was signed.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp after which this snapshot MUST NOT be cached.

jti.description: JTI of the revoked TCT: lowercase UUID v4 in the RFC-AITP-0005 §2.2 layout.

revoked_at.description: Unix timestamp when the issuing peer revoked this TCT.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason. Not used in trust decisions.

entries.description: Revoked-entry records. MAY be empty — an empty list is itself a signed assertion that nothing has been revoked, defending against suppression of fresher snapshots.

extensions.description: Optional extension namespace per RFC-AITP-0001 §7 and RFC-AITP-0012. Unknown keys inside `extensions` MUST be ignored; unknown fields outside it are rejected by this schema.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url signature (RFC 4648 §5) by the issuing peer over the JCS-canonical bytes (RFC 8785) of the INNER `revocation_list` body. This object is the transport envelope: the `revocation_list` key names the artifact for routing and is NOT part of the signing bytes, and `signature` is a sibling of the body rather than a member of it, so nothing is removed before canonicalizing (RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.1, RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5). A verifier MUST unwrap to the inner object before computing the signing input. `schemas/conformance/known-answer/jcs-sha256.json` (`kat-revocation-001`) pins that signing input, and `known-answer/signed-examples/revocation/` carries a real signature over it that conformant implementations MUST verify as committed, without re-minting. A runtime-served snapshot MUST also carry this field.
